articles.title: Experience: I didn’t know I was pregnant until I gave birth
articles.summary: There’d been no morning sickness, cravings or tiredness. My mum didn’t believe I’d had a baby – even after seeing her on FaceTime. When I was 19, I went to college in Texas, where I met my ­boyfriend Preston. It was 2023 and I had big plans.
body: In May 2025, I took a trip to London, returning to campus in August after the summer holidays. I noticed I was slowly gaining weight; by January this year I’d gained 10lb. I put it down to my late-night snacking and lack of exercise.
But then on 20 February, after I had returned to my apartment following my morning class, I felt cramps in my lower stomach. At 1pm, I took some ibuprofen.

At 6.20pm, I felt a sudden urge to go to the toilet. After sitting there for a while with nothing happening, I stood up, assuming I was constipated. Then, I felt something strange happening between my legs. I looked down and saw something bulging out of me. I froze. I thought it was a tumour and that I was going to die.

But then I felt the urge to push – and suddenly there was a baby’s head between my thighs. I was terrified, but primal instinct took over. I waddled to my bedroom and grabbed a clean towel. I laid it down and dropped to my hands and knees. The adrenaline was pumping so hard that I don’t remember feeling pain. Three quick pushes later, I was able to grab my baby. Laying her on the floor in front of me, I rubbed her chest to help her cry. I did it all without thinking. Then I called 911.
points: There’d been no morning sickness, cravings or tiredness.

articles.title: Helen Goh’s recipe for brown butter apple and blackberry bars | The sweet spot
articles.summary: A bar for the bountiful season, with a rubbly oat crust, a soft fruit filling and a crisp topping. September is always a wistful time for me. Summer has all but slipped away, the days are noticeably shorter and the children are heading back to school.
body: These will keep for up to three days in an airtight container, and also freeze well, wrapped individually for convenience.

Grease and line a 20cm x 30cm baking tin with greaseproof paper, leaving enough overhang to help lift out the bars later. Put the butter in a medium saucepan on a medium heat and cook, swirling the pan occasionally, for about five minutes, until it smells nutty and the milk solids turn a deep golden brown. Take off the heat, stir in the anise seeds, if using, then leave to cool for five minutes.

Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan)/390F/gas 6. Meanwhile, mix the plain flour, rolled oats, oat flour, brown sugar and salt in a large bowl. Pour over the browned butter, including all the toasted milk solids, and mix until evenly moistened. The mixture should resemble damp sand and hold together when squeezed.

Reserve about 350g of the crumb mix for the topping, then tip the rest into the lined tin, pressing firmly into an even layer; use the base of a measuring cup or back of a spoon. This will help the bars hold together neatly when slicing. Bake for 18 minutes, until lightly golden around the edges.

articles.title: Your home organization can actually look stylish. These 27 designer-approved solutions are proof
articles.summary: If you feel like you’re drowning in stuff and can’t find anything you need, there’s a box (or basket) for that. 11 products our writers rely on to organize and declutter. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Look around your house and be honest: are you drowning in stuff? I know I am. Between a toddler, one on the way, two cats and a personal inability to throw out junk “just in case”, it’s rare I see the actual surface of my floor or countertops.

Without a home organization system that works for you, the sheer amount of objects you have accumulated throughout the years can quickly overrun your home. Many of us tend to put away stuff “for now”, only for our closets and cabinets to fill up, preventing us from seeing what we own. “If you can’t find something, it can feel easier to order another one than to spend 20 minutes searching,” Amy Berryhill, a professional organizer and owner of Spiffy Chicks, said.

The best way to make space for everything you need is to make intentional – and stylish! – choices about how you organize your home. “We like to think about organization as an extension of the design process, finding ways to give everyday items a designated home without sacrificing beauty,” said Audrey Scheck, an interior designer and founder of Audrey Scheck Design.

articles.title: The Best Liquid Blushes That Offer a Natural, Skin-Like Flush
articles.summary: In search of a rosy cheek? Three traits define the best liquid blush: buildable, lightweight, and long-wearing. We included options from Saie, Armani Beauty, and more.
body: Not so long ago, blush played a supporting role—the step you skipped when running late, a swipe of powder somewhere near the cheekbone, if that. Too much, too rosy, too eighties. Then it came back with a vengeance: worn higher on the face, in brighter shades, in placements that a decade ago you might’ve deemed a mistake (blush blindness, we’ve all been there). The format leading the return is liquid: It melts into skin, builds a dot at a time, blends with a fingertip, and reads like a natural flush rather than ‘makeup’.

The formulas have caught up, too. Early liquid blushes could be unforgiving—“either extremely pigmented, difficult to blend, or so emollient that they disrupted the complexion underneath,” Jaikaran says. “This is where the term ‘blush blindness’ came from.” The new generation gives you more playtime to blend and sets down better. Wear time has stretched to what Spickard describes as formulas “that almost stain” and ingredients now read like serums and include skin-loving factors like hyaluronic acid, niacinamide, ceramides, peptides, and more. Even the delivery system keeps evolving, from mousses and gels to tints.
points: Three traits define the best liquid blush: buildable, lightweight, and long-wearing.

articles.summary: As the 2026 Venice Film Festival kicks off this week, all eyes will be on the red carpet—with the likes of George and Amal Clooney, Claire Foy, and Robert Pattinson arriving in the Italian city. See all the best fashion from Venice Film Festival so far.
body: Red carpet lovers, it’s your lucky day: The 2026 Venice Film Festival has officially arrived.

The film roster for this year’s festival has plenty of buzzy projects to take in: Among them is Martin McDonagh’s Oscar-tipped black comedy Wild Horse Nine; Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime; a Robert Pattinson-led portrait of To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen; and Bunker, Florian Zeller’s marital drama starring Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

Better year, however, is what all of these A-listers will be wearing on the step and repeat for the splashy premieres. This is, after all, the festival that last year offered the first glimpses of new-era Chanel, Dior, Versace and Bottega Veneta before their respective runway debuts, and which has given us Lady Gaga’s feathered Valentino couture gown in 2018 and Zendaya’s wet-look Balmain dress in 2021, among other standout moments.

articles.summary: Featuring Dollywood day trips, mountain views, and plenty of leaf-peeping
body: Frequently named the most visited national park in the US, Great Smoky Mountains have universal appeal—travelers come from all over the country (and the world) to enjoy the natural beauty of this part of North Carolina and Tennessee. Hikers, anglers, photographers, road-trippers, birders, families, and thrill-seekers can all find reasons to make the trek. Whether you want to see the namesake fog blanketing the peaks—many of which tower well over 6,000 feet—breathe in the crisp air, or glimpse the famous wildflowers and fall foliage, there’s plenty to do, and some excellent places to spend the night once you get here.

articles.title: The Best Citrus Perfumes Are Surprisingly Versatile
articles.summary: According to experts, citrus pairs beautifully with other notes, making the best citrus fragrances by Dior, Guerlain, and more surprisingly versatile.
body: If fruity fragrances lean too sweet for your liking and clean scents feel too minimalist, citrus perfumes may be the ideal middle ground. A well-crafted citrus scent doesn’t smell like your average multisurface cleaning spray or a simple squeeze of lemon; it’s more nuanced than that.

“A fruity perfume and a citrus-forward perfume speak entirely different languages on the skin,” Guerlain perfume creation director and perfumer Delphine Jelk tells Vogue. “A fruity fragrance is about lushness, roundness, and indulgence and often leans gourmand or soft. Citrus, on the other hand, is about light, energy, and crispness. Citrus notes come from the zests—the peel—so they offer an immediate, sparkling bite, an awakening of the senses.”

Citrus notes are remarkably versatile, according to Jelk. “Citrus marries beautifully with aromatic herbs like basil, mint, or thyme, which heightens its natural green facet,” she says, noting that citrus can work just as well with unexpected pairings, such as spices. She adds that woody, ambery, and musky bases create “gorgeous tension between a bright opening and a deep, sensual dry-down.” Scroll on to discover Vogue ’s favorite citrus perfumes.
points: According to experts, citrus pairs beautifully with other notes, making the best citrus fragrances by Dior, Guerlain, and more surprisingly versatile.
